title: Compact benchmark result store + comparison canvas and triage playbook
creator: Maya Liu
description: Implement a compact, query-friendly storage layer for benchmark/time-series artifacts plus a lightweight comparison canvas UI and an operator-focused anomaly triage playbook. Deliverables: (1) a tersely indexed result store that optimizes for frequent p95 and tokens/sec lookups and fingerprint-based regression grouping; (2) an interactive comparison canvas that supports pairwise overlay, histogram diff, and deltas by model variant/quantization/hardware; (3) a documented triage workflow with playbook runbooks and automation hooks for alerting and suggested root-cause buckets.
acceptance_criteria: Result store supports efficient time-range queries for p50/p95/tokens_per_sec and returns top-10 regressions by delta in <500ms for 90% of queries
Comparison canvas renders pairwise time-aligned overlays and delta histograms for two benchmark runs within 2s for median users
Regression grouping by fingerprint (prompt hashing + exemplar embeddings) surface reduces duplicate alerts by >=40% in internal tests
Triage playbook includes RBAC owners, severity mapping, automatic triage suggestions, and links to infra metrics (GPU utilization, kernel selection logs)
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Index-first vs blob-first: chose compact columnar index (time-series + small metadata) with cold blob store for raw traces to keep fast queries on common aggregates
Fingerprinting: use 64-bit locality-preserving hash + sample embedding signature to avoid bloom filter false positives; accepts slight risk of collisions but reduces grouping noise
Retention: keep high-resolution traces for 30 days, aggregated rollups for 1 year to balance disk costs vs triage fidelity
UI complexity: prefer an opinionated comparison canvas (limited toggle set) over a fully generic plotting studio to speed iteration and avoid user paralysis
implementation_notes: Storage: new table `bench_series_compact` in timeseries DB (schema: run_id, model_variant, hw_tier, metric, time_bucket, value, fingerprint, rollup_key)
Serialization: values compressed with ZSTD level 3 and delta-encoded per-run for tokens/sec and latencies
API: add endpoints /bench/v1/compare and /bench/v1/top-regressions with query params (metric, window, baseline_run_id, target_run_id)
UI: React canvas component integrated into Console -> Benchmarks. Use canvas-level WebSocket for streaming live comparisons
Alerting: wire comparison deltas into existing anomaly-detector; add confidence score and suggested triage category tags
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: spike completed comparing Postgres timeseries vs ClickHouse column store for our query patterns. ClickHouse favored for aggregate-heavy queries.
2026-02-18: prototype index schema implemented and microbenchmarks show 3x faster p95 lookups vs existing blob store on sample dataset (10M rows).
2026-02-26: initial React canvas wireframe reviewed by PM + Design (Julia Park). Feedback: surface baseline selection and auto-align by prompt fingerprint by default.
2026-03-03: integration test failing intermittently when combining fingerprint grouping with model-variant fallbacks; root cause likely upstream canonicalization bug (ENG-84912 referenced).
2026-03-10: backend API stabilized; deployed to staging. Beginning UI integration tests and triage doc drafting.
2026-03-12: triage playbook draft reviewed by oncall perf (Ravi Patel) and ML infra (Aisha Khan). Added an automatic checklist for kernel-selection, batch-size, and cache-hit-rate checks.
review_feedback: Julia Park (Design): keep comparison canvas controls compact; prioritize delta histogram and p95 timeline. Remove free-form plotting in MVP.
Ravi Patel (SRE): add GPU kernel logs correlation in triage view; include a link that pre-fills a trace query with time window from regression event.
Aisha Khan (ML Infra): recommend retaining raw KV-cache hit logs for 7 days even if traces age out to help intermittent cache-related regressions
Security (Lara Voss): ensure any run artifacts with customer prompts are automatically redacted before long-term storage (we will add redaction hook in ingestion pipeline)
next_steps: Finish frontend compare canvas implementation and hookup /bench/v1/compare streaming endpoint
Complete ClickHouse schema migration and fill initial rollups for prod shard 3
Add automation to anomaly-detector to add suggested triage tags and a first-pass root-cause bucket
Run end-to-end fault injection: simulate kernel fallback, quantization variant mismatch, and network egress to validate triage playbook steps
notes_for_oncall: When an alert fires with confidence >0.7, open comparison canvas with baseline pinned to last-successful-run; follow triage checklist
If triage indicates kernel selection regression, escalate to ML Infra and add tag 'kernel-regression' to incident.
If fingerprint grouping returns >10 unique groups for same prompt hash, toggle to sample-mode to inspect exemplar prompts and check redaction pipeline
